unchanged since bda7c27 (git diff checked); round-14 evidence: Judged against the contract: stationary_bootstrap_indices(n_obs, mean_block, rng) 'start at a uniform index; at each later step, with probability 1/mean_block start a new block at a uniform index, otherwise move to (previous + 1) mod n_obs'. The standard error of a share is sqrt(0.2 x 0.8 / 10000) = 0.004, so the tolerance is 5 standard errors (false-failure probability about 1e-6 per index). rows.evidence: unchanged since bda7c27 (git diff checked); round-14 evidence: Round 14, new card. Back: '65% of the 452 anomalies in their data library cannot clear the single-test hurdle of 1.96, with microcaps mitigated via NYSE breakpoints and value-weighted returns.' Hou, Xue and Zhang (RFS 33(5), DOI 10.1093/rfs/hhy131), Crossref abstract (read): 'With microcaps mitigated via NYSE breakpoints and value-weighted returns, 65% of the 452 anomalies in our extensive data library, including 96% of the trading frictions category, cannot clear the single test hurdle of the absolute t-value of 1.96.' Match, including 'in their data library' and the scope. The front's 'under which choices' is answered by the scope. The L03 span (B, Abstract) says the same ('65% of 452 anomalies cannot clear the single-test hurdle of 1.96', 'The full debate belongs to F5'). Counter-evidence: the 11 citing works dated 2025-2026 with anomaly, replication, false-discovery or factor titles (r14/counter/hou2018replicating.json: 971 citing works, 40 examined, 21 with abstracts) were checked on their Crossref abstracts: none mentions Hou, microcaps, NYSE, the 65% figure or the 1.96 hurdle (Correlated False Discoveries, SSRN 2025, has an empty abstract and was not read). The published counter to the replication conclusion is Jensen, Kelly and Pedersen (J Finance 78(5), 2025 abstract: 'The majority of asset pricing factors ... can be replicated'), named in the same L03 §8 paragraph, not on the card. The card contests no number; the L03 page names the counter. PASS, with the freshness flag for the 2025 SSRN paper.

mutants.description: Benjamini-Hochberg run step-down: stops at the first ordered p-value above its line instead of taking the largest passing k.
Benjamini-Hochberg returns the rejection mask in sorted (rank) order instead of the input order.
Benjamini-Hochberg uses a strict inequality p_(k) < kq/m, so a p-value exactly on its line is not rejected.
sample_kurtosis returns excess kurtosis m4/m2**2 - 3 (the scipy default) where the contract requires raw kurtosis.
Sharpe-ratio standard error divides the variance bracket by n instead of n - 1.
Sharpe-ratio standard error uses (kurtosis - 3)/4 in the bracket, mixing the excess-kurtosis form with raw kurtosis.
Deflated Sharpe ratio takes the population variance (ddof=0) of the trial Sharpe ratios instead of ddof=1.
expected_max_sharpe at N = 1 returns 0.0 instead of sr_mean (forgets the shift when there is no selection).
Stationary bootstrap never wraps around: a block that would run past the last period starts a new block instead of continuing at index 0.
Stationary bootstrap uses mean_block as the restart probability (1/p in place of p), so every step starts a new block.
Romano-Wolf resamples each strategy with its own bootstrap index vector, breaking the cross-sectional dependence.
Romano-Wolf is not studentized: it compares raw mean differentials with centred bootstrap means instead of t-statistics.
Step-down rejects hypotheses with t_obs >= c instead of t_obs > c.
Step-down critical value is np.quantile(maxima, 1 - alpha) with linear interpolation instead of the ceil((1-alpha)B)-th order statistic.
Step-down critical value uses the floor((1-alpha)B)-th order statistic instead of the ceil((1-alpha)B)-th.
Step-down never recomputes the critical value: one max-T critical value over all hypotheses (single-step test).
PBO counts logits < 0 instead of logits <= 0, so a median out-of-sample rank is not counted as overfit.
CSCV drops the newest T mod S rows instead of the oldest.
CSCV out-of-sample rank ignores ties (1 + #lower, a 'min' rank) instead of the average rank with +0.5 per tie.
integrity_report feeds Benjamini-Hochberg two-sided p-values 2(1 - Phi(|t|)) instead of one-sided p-values for H0: mean <= 0.
integrity_report passes n_blocks to CSCV unchanged instead of reducing it to the largest even number <= min(n_blocks, T).
Uses scipy.stats.norm for the PSR's normal CDF, a dependency the A8 contract forbids (NumPy and the standard library only).
CSCV omits the half-sample rule: with (T - T mod S) / 2 < 2 it runs on one-period half-samples instead of raising ValueError.
Romano-Wolf studentizes a constant resampled column by np.finfo(float).tiny instead of the column's sample standard deviation.
Romano-Wolf discards every bootstrap draw in which a resampled column is constant, instead of studentizing it by the column's sample standard deviation.
integrity_report runs on fewer than 4 periods and reports pbo = nan instead of raising ValueError.
Series validation flattens a two-dimensional input with ravel() instead of raising ValueError.
Romano-Wolf studentizes every bootstrap draw by the full-sample standard deviation instead of the draw's own std(d*_k, ddof=1).
Romano-Wolf computes the bootstrap draws' standard deviations with np.std's default ddof=0, while the observed statistics use ddof=1.
CSCV's subsample Sharpe metric is plain mean / std, ignoring the contract's rule for a constant subsample (0.0 if its mean is 0, +-inf by the sign of the mean otherwise).
Stationary bootstrap starts the first block at index 0 instead of at a uniform random index.
sample_skewness and sample_kurtosis skip the series validation, so a two-dimensional or non-finite input returns a number instead of raising ValueError.
sharpe_ratio detects zero variance with std(x, ddof=1) == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic series returns a huge Sharpe ratio instead of raising ValueError.
romano_wolf omits the constant-column check, so a column with all values equal is studentized by its (zero or tiny) standard deviation instead of raising ValueError.
romano_wolf detects a constant resampled column with std(d*_k, ddof=1) == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic resample is divided by a tiny floating-point standard deviation.
CSCV's subsample metric detects a constant subsample with std == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic subsample gets a huge finite Sharpe ratio instead of +-inf.
CSCV floors the subsample standard deviation at 1e-12 to avoid dividing by zero, so a constant non-zero subsample gets a large finite metric instead of +-inf.
sample_skewness and sample_kurtosis detect zero variance with m2 == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic series returns a meaningless number instead of raising ValueError.
stationary_bootstrap_indices does not validate mean_block, so mean_block < 1 (a restart probability above one) returns indices instead of raising ValueError.
sample_skewness and sample_kurtosis compute their moments on the raw series (only the Sharpe ratio is rescaled), so a fourth power overflows at 1e155 and a square underflows at 2**-1000.

romano_wolf rescales the whole differentials matrix by the one power of two of its largest absolute value instead of each column by its own, so a column far smaller than the largest underflows when squared.
romano_wolf creates rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) inside the bootstrap loop, so every draw reuses the same index vector instead of drawing n_boot vectors in order from one generator.

romano_wolf draws all n_boot index vectors at once from one generator (vectorized) instead of calling stationary_bootstrap_indices(T, mean_block, rng) once per draw in order, as the contract now requires.
CSCV scores every constant subsample 0.0 (zero variance read as zero Sharpe ratio) instead of +-inf by the sign of its value.

romano_wolf detects a constant column of differentials with std(d_k, ddof=1) == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic column is studentized by a tiny standard deviation instead of raising ValueError.
stationary_bootstrap_indices checks only mean_block < 1, so a NaN mean_block (every comparison False) passes and yields one block instead of raising ValueError.
sharpe_ratio_std squares the Sharpe ratio with sharpe**2, so a huge Sharpe ratio raises OverflowError instead of the contract's ValueError for a variance bracket that overflows.
romano_wolf does not validate alpha (it calls the step-down loop directly), so alpha outside (0, 1) returns decisions instead of raising ValueError.
deflated_sharpe_ratio takes np.var(trial_sharpes, ddof=1) on the raw values, so a variance beyond the largest float warns and returns instead of raising ValueError.

romano_wolf studentizes each resample in its column's scale (rescales the column once, not the resample), so a resample of values far smaller than its column's largest has a square that underflows and a zero standard deviation.

CSCV computes each subsample's Sharpe ratio in its configuration's full-sample scale (rescales each column once, not each subsample), so a subsample of values far smaller than the column's largest has a zero standard deviation.
benjamini_hochberg checks the p-value range with comparisons only, so a NaN p-value (every comparison False) passes and is never rejected instead of raising ValueError.
probabilistic_sharpe_ratio rejects only a NaN benchmark (math.isnan), so an infinite sr_benchmark returns 0.0 or 1.0 instead of raising ValueError.
The power-of-two rescaling takes its exponent from the largest value (x.max()) instead of the largest absolute value, so a series dominated by a large negative return overflows when it is 'rescaled'.
romano_wolf seeds a fresh generator for every bootstrap draw (np.random.default_rng([seed, b])) instead of drawing all n_boot index vectors in order from the single rng = np.random.default_rng(seed).
CSCV scores every constant nonzero subsample +inf, ignoring its sign, so a configuration that loses the same amount every period looks like the best in-sample.
romano_wolf studentizes a constant resampled column by the column's population standard deviation (np.std default ddof=0) instead of std(d_k, ddof=1).
Integer arguments are checked with int(x) != x, so an infinite n_obs, n_trials, n_boot or n_blocks raises OverflowError instead of ValueError.
expected_max_sharpe evaluates the textbook Phi^-1(1 - 1/N), which is infinite once 1 - 1/N rounds to 1 (N beyond 2**53), instead of -Phi^-1(1/N).
sharpe_ratio_std does arithmetic on its scalar arguments as given, so a NumPy float64 Sharpe ratio whose square overflows raises a RuntimeWarning instead of the contract's ValueError.
TrialSet casts selected and periods_per_year with int() before validating them, so a fractional selected silently picks the column below it.

romano_wolf re-expresses the column mean in the resample's scale without guarding the overflow, so a column spanning more than 2**1024 between its largest value and a resample's largest value warns instead of giving the contract's -inf statistic.

probabilistic_sharpe_ratio subtracts a NumPy-scalar benchmark without converting it with float(), so an extreme np.float64 benchmark raises an overflow RuntimeWarning.

The power-of-two rescaling divides by 2.0**e instead of calling np.ldexp, so a series whose largest absolute value is at least 2**1023 (about 9e307) overflows the divisor to inf with a RuntimeWarning.

romano_wolf guards the overflow of the re-expressed column mean but not of the studentized difference, so a resample far smaller than its column warns (overflow in divide) instead of giving the contract's quiet +-inf statistic.

integrity_report computes the trials' t-statistics for the BH p-values on the unscaled returns, so a trial set of tiny or huge returns (2**-600 or 2**600 times ordinary ones) underflows or overflows its variances and warns.
integrity_report does not forward its seed, so its Romano-Wolf bootstrap is always drawn from np.random.default_rng(0) whatever seed the caller passes.
integrity_report does not forward alpha, so its Romano-Wolf rejections always use romano_wolf's default level 0.05 whatever alpha the caller passes.
deflated_sharpe_ratio applies the zero-variance rule of a return series to trial_sharpes, so equal trial Sharpe ratios (variance 0, so SR0 = 0) raise ValueError instead of giving the PSR against 0.
integrity_report validates q but runs Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha, the StepM level, so bh_rejections ignore the caller's q.
integrity_report does not forward mean_block, so its Romano-Wolf bootstrap always uses romano_wolf's default mean block length 10 whatever the caller passes.
integrity_report computes the trials' t-statistics for the BH p-values with np.std's default ddof=0 instead of std(ddof=1).

Step-down uses each hypothesis's own bootstrap quantile (the ceil((1-alpha)B)-th smallest t*_bk of column k) instead of the quantile of the maximum over the active set, so it controls no family-wise error.
CSCV forms its S blocks by interleaving rows (block i holds rows i, i+S, i+2S, ...) instead of consecutive runs of periods.
integrity_report annualizes the selected Sharpe ratio by multiplying by periods_per_year instead of its square root.
Stationary bootstrap draws block starts with rng.integers(0, n - 1), an exclusive upper bound one too low, so the last period never starts a block.
expected_max_sharpe hard-codes Lesson 7 Example 3.2's bracket 2.1895 for N = 40 trials instead of evaluating the formula at the given N.
deflated_sharpe_ratio ignores an explicit n_trials and always deflates by len(trial_sharpes).
probabilistic_sharpe_ratio subtracts in the wrong order, Phi((SR* - SR)/se), so it returns one minus the PSR.
integrity_report ignores TrialSet.selected and reports on the trial with the highest Sharpe ratio, which is only the proposed strategy when the proposal is the in-sample best.
stepdown_rejections removes each rejected hypothesis from the maximum by writing -inf into its column of the caller's t_boot, so the caller's bootstrap matrix is mutated.
CSCV breaks an in-sample tie for the best configuration in favour of the highest index instead of the lowest.
integrity_report prints a one-line summary of its result, a leftover debugging statement the contract forbids.
romano_wolf multiplies the caller's differentials matrix by its per-column power of two in place, so the caller's data change although every decision stays the same.
benjamini_hochberg sorts the caller's p-value array in place after taking its ordering, so the caller's array is mutated although the returned mask is right.
integrity_report annualizes the selected Sharpe ratio with a hard-coded sqrt(252), ignoring the trial set's periods_per_year.
TrialSet.from_backtest takes the in-sample best column as selected instead of the backtest result's own selected attribute.
benjamini_hochberg, stepdown_rejections and romano_wolf accept a level of exactly 1 (0 < level <= 1), although the contract requires 0 < q < 1 and 0 < alpha < 1.
integrity_report requires T > 4 instead of T >= 4, so the smallest trial set the contract allows (four periods, two-period CSCV halves) raises ValueError.
stationary_bootstrap_indices rejects mean_block == 1 (requires > 1), although the contract allows any mean_block >= 1, which is the iid bootstrap.
integrity_report takes each trial's p-value as 1 - PSR(trial, 0), the skewness-and-kurtosis-adjusted tail, instead of the contract's 1 - Phi(mean / (std / sqrt(T))).
The step-down loop compares absolute statistics, |t| against the maximum of |t*|, as for a two-sided test, although each hypothesis is one-sided (E[d] <= 0).
probability_of_backtest_overfitting evaluates only the first 500 splits in itertools order to save time, so a PBO with 12 or more blocks (924 or more splits) is not the share over all of them.
CSCV ranks configurations by their mean return instead of their Sharpe ratio, in sample and out of sample.
integrity_report returns the Benjamini-Hochberg mask in order of increasing p-value instead of the trials' column order.
benjamini_hochberg returns a stored mask when it recognises the seed-0 instance's p-values and otherwise uses the step-down rule (stop at the first p-value above its line).
integrity_report builds each trial's t-statistic for the p-values with sqrt(T - 1) in the standard error instead of sqrt(T).
stationary_bootstrap_indices truncates mean_block to an integer with int(), so a mean block of 2.5 behaves as 2.
Series validation requires at least 3 observations instead of 2, so a series of exactly two observations raises ValueError.
romano_wolf requires n_boot >= 2 instead of n_boot >= 1, so a single bootstrap draw raises ValueError.
stepdown_rejections requires B >= 2 bootstrap draws instead of B >= 1.
stationary_bootstrap_indices requires n_obs >= 2 instead of n_obs >= 1.
deflated_sharpe_ratio requires at least 3 trial Sharpe ratios instead of 2.
deflated_sharpe_ratio requires an explicit n_trials of at least 2, so n_trials = 1 (a valid single-trial deflation, SR0 = 0) raises ValueError.
sharpe_ratio_std requires n_obs >= 3 instead of n_obs >= 2, so the smallest sample the contract allows raises ValueError.
PBOResult, TrialSet and IntegrityReport are plain dataclasses, not frozen=True as the contract says, so their fields can be reassigned.
benjamini_hochberg, stepdown_rejections and romano_wolf return a Python list of bools instead of the NDArray[np.bool_] the contract names.
benjamini_hochberg requires 0 < p < 1, so a p-value of exactly 0 or exactly 1 raises ValueError although the contract allows [0, 1].
romano_wolf does not centre the bootstrap statistics at the observed mean: t*_bk = mean(d*_k) / (std(d*_k, ddof=1) / sqrt(T)).
romano_wolf runs the step-down at alpha / 2 (a two-sided level) although each hypothesis is one-sided.
integrity_report does not forward n_boot, so its Romano-Wolf bootstrap always uses 1000 draws.
TrialSet bounds selected by 0 <= selected < N - 1 (an off-by-one), so the last column cannot be the proposed strategy.
integrity_report defaults to n_blocks = 8 instead of the contract's 16.
integrity_report defaults to n_boot = 500 instead of the contract's 1000.
romano_wolf defaults to mean_block = 5.0 instead of the contract's 10.0.
probability_of_backtest_overfitting defaults to n_blocks = 8 instead of the contract's 16.
integrity_report defaults to seed = 1 instead of the contract's 0.
romano_wolf defaults to alpha = 0.10 instead of the contract's 0.05.

stationary_bootstrap_indices cuts the resample into fixed blocks of round(mean_block) periods (a moving-block bootstrap), instead of geometric block lengths that restart with probability 1/mean_block.
benjamini_hochberg leaves the p-values equal to 1 out of the number of hypotheses m, as if they were not tests, so the step-up lines use the smaller count.
benjamini_hochberg counts each distinct p-value once in m (np.unique), so ties among rounded p-values shrink the number of hypotheses in the step-up lines.
romano_wolf returns its decision vector in reverse column order, an indexing error that leaves each decision with the wrong strategy when there are several columns.
romano_wolf squeezes its decision vector with np.squeeze, so a single differentials column returns a 0-d array rather than one boolean per column.
stepdown_rejections takes its critical value as np.quantile(maxima, 1 - alpha, method='higher') instead of the ceil((1-alpha)B)-th order statistic.
sample_kurtosis divides the fourth central moment by the squared sample variance with ddof=1 (m4 over s**4), mixing the sample and the moment estimators.
stationary_bootstrap_indices draws every block start after the first from periods 1..n-1, so period 0 is never the start of a new block (an off-by-one in the integers bound).
expected_max_sharpe swaps the Euler-Mascheroni weights: gamma multiplies the 1/N quantile and 1 - gamma the 1/(N e) quantile.
stationary_bootstrap_indices starts a new block with probability 1/(mean_block + 1), an off-by-one in the block-length parameter.
CSCV's out-of-sample rank counts the chosen configuration as one of its own ties, so every rank is 0.5 too high.
Romano-Wolf step-down takes its critical value from the maxima over all hypotheses, not over the ones still active.
Step-down critical value is the (floor((1-alpha) B) + 1)-th order statistic, one rank above the contract's ceil((1-alpha) B)-th when (1-alpha) B is an integer.
Stationary bootstrap wraps the time index modulo n_obs - 1, so the last period is never drawn after the first block start.
Romano-Wolf's bootstrap statistics divide by sqrt(T - 1), the T - 1 convention of the Sharpe-ratio standard error carried into the t* draws, while the observed statistics keep sqrt(T).
probabilistic_sharpe_ratio computes its standard error with T - 1 periods instead of T, an off-by-one in the sample size.
sharpe_ratio_std adds the skewness term (+skew*SR) to the variance bracket instead of subtracting it, a sign error in the non-normal standard error.
Romano-Wolf's constant-resample branch takes the means from the unscaled differentials but the standard error from the rescaled ones, so units mix whenever a column is not near unit magnitude.
CSCV's out-of-sample rank takes the largest rank of a tie (1 + #lower + #others equal) instead of the average rank, so tied configurations are ranked too high.
Benjamini-Hochberg compares every ordered p-value with the Bonferroni line q/m instead of the rank line kq/m, so the step-up rejects by the largest p-value under q/m.
CSCV keeps only the splits whose in-sample half contains block 0, half of the C(S, S/2) splits, so the logit distribution is estimated from a subset of the splits.
The expected maximum uses Phi^-1(1 - 1/(N+1)) in place of Phi^-1(1 - 1/N) in its first term, an off-by-one in the number of trials.

sample_skewness returns the bias-corrected adjusted Fisher-Pearson estimator g1 * sqrt(n(n-1))/(n-2) instead of the moment estimator m3 / m2**1.5, so the skewness fed to the PSR and to the Sharpe ratio's standard error is inflated.

CSCV scores the in-sample winner on the same blocks it was chosen from (the out-of-sample set is the in-sample half, the complement forgotten), so the winner always ranks first out of sample and the PBO is zero.

expected_max_sharpe multiplies the z-score by sr_variance, the variance of the Sharpe estimates, instead of its square root, so the expected maximum scales with the variance and the DSR's benchmark SR0 is too small when the variance is below one.
Stationary bootstrap draws block starts from 0..n-2 (rng.integers(0, n - 1)), so the last period never starts a block.
DSR benchmark is the mean of the trial Sharpe ratios (the average trial) instead of their expected maximum under the null.
PSR returns the one-sided p-value 1 - Phi(z) instead of Phi(z), the probability that the true Sharpe ratio exceeds the benchmark.
CSCV relative rank divides by the number of strategies N instead of N + 1, so the logit of the top rank is infinite and the logits differ from the definition.
